title: Clinical and Electrophysiological Heterogeneity in Adult Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease
official: Clinical and Electrophysiological Heterogeneity in Adult Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease: An Observational Study of the Relationships Between CMTES-v2, Nerve Conduction Parameters, and Functional Capacity
summary: CMT-PROFILE is a single-center, cross-sectional observational study involving adults with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT). The study will investigate the association between clinical disease severity, measured using the CMT Examination Score version 2 (CMTES-v2), and motor electrophysiological parameters, including compound muscle action potential (CMAP) amplitudes and motor nerve conduction velocities. Secondary objectives include characterizing clinical-electrophysiological concordance, comparing functional capacity, muscle strength and mobility across concordance groups, and exploring demographic, clinical, biological and genetic factors associated with variability in disease expression. Approximately 250 patients are planned for inclusion. All assessments will be performed at a single reference time point (M0), with no longitudinal follow-up.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 years or older.
* Diagnosis of peripheral sensory polyneuropathy.
* Classification as length-dependent (LDN) or non-length-dependent (NLDN) based on clinical and electrophysiological findings.
* Available nerve conduction study including sural and radial sensory nerve amplitudes allowing calculation of the SRAR.
* Evaluated at the Peripheral Neuromuscular Rare Disease Reference Center, Nice University Hospital, between January 2013 and July 2026.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Missing or incomplete clinical or electrophysiological data preventing SRAR calculation.
* Unclassifiable neuropathy phenotype.
* Technical factors affecting the reliability of nerve conduction studies.
